task.title: Offline escrow rights ledger
task.specification: config={initial:nonnegative integer,grants:{transferId:positive integer}}. Start available=initial,spent=0. Events receive/send/spend have {type,id,amount:positive integer}; ack/cancel have {type,id}. Receive accepts only a listed grant with exactly its amount, adds rights once; matching repeat is duplicate, all other receives invalid. A send or spend with a fresh ID succeeds only if available>=amount, debits immediately, and is recorded permanently; insufficient attempts are not recorded. Matching recorded repeat is duplicate and changed amount is conflict. Spend increases spent. Send reserves an outgoing transfer pending until ack (permanently delivered) or cancel (refund once). Ack/cancel only changes a currently pending send; otherwise ignored. ID namespaces are separate for receives, sends and spends. Output {status,available,spent,pending,received}, sorted ID arrays. Status is accepted,duplicate,conflict,insufficient,invalid,or ignored. Delivery acknowledgment never refunds rights. Return one JSON output per event; state is opaque JSON, initially null. Objects in outputs have exactly the documented keys; map keys are unordered, arrays are ordered. Sorted/lexicographic string order compares Unicode scalar values (code points), with a shorter prefix first. Numeric inputs/values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values (no unpaired surrogates). Decoded imported values outside these limits are invalid frames. There are at most 48 events. Unknown/invalid operations have the behavior below. Each instance starts fresh. Hidden ordinary cases vary legal values; boundary cases emphasize equality, empty data and duplicates; adversarial cases reorder and conflict; shift cases use longer traces and more identities within the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
matchedCard.relation: The origin and original arrangement of records preserve relationships that can be lost when the same contents are rearranged arbitrarily. A later description or arrangement is distinct from evidence of the organization in which the records were produced.
assumptions: The origin or original order is known or supported by evidence.
Relationships among records contribute to their interpretation.
matchedCard.boundary: Original order can be lost or disrupted. A newly devised arrangement does not establish that it was the historical arrangement, and provenance does not make every recorded claim true.
matchedCard.source_fact: The National Archives explains provenance, preserving or restoring original order, and devising arrangements when necessary, emphasizing the evidential significance of context.

shuffledCard.label: Seed banking
shuffledCard.relation: Preserving a reserve and preserving its ability to reactivate are different conditions. Suitable material remains in controlled storage, while periodic sample recovery provides evidence of continued viability. Duplicate holdings reduce dependence on one location.
assumptions: The material tolerates the chosen storage treatment.
Samples provide relevant evidence about the collection they represent.
Duplicate collections remain identifiable as corresponding holdings.
shuffledCard.boundary: Some material cannot survive drying or freezing. Successful retention alone does not demonstrate viability, and sampled viability is not certainty about every stored item.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Kew stores suitable dried seeds in cold vaults, periodically tests germination, and commonly duplicates holdings in their country of origin. Some seeds do not tolerate conventional storage.

sources.title: How to preserve seeds for the future

initial.explanation: Rule: every accepted debit lowers available exactly once; every accepted receive raises it exactly once; only a pending send cancellation refunds its debit. I use this conservation rule while preserving independent ID namespaces. A counterexample is a duplicate spend changing available again, which violates one-time debit.
initial.mapping: available, spent, pending, received, and operation records map directly to the ledger state; pending sends are refundable records, while delivered sends remain permanently debited.
initial.assumptions: Malformed operations are invalid; malformed acknowledgments/cancellations are ignored only when structurally valid IDs are absent from pending sends. IDs are strings and amounts are safe positive integers.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let s=null;for(let i=0;i<output.length;i++){let r=solve({config:input.config,state:s,event:input.events[i]});if(!eq(r.output,output[i]))return false;s=r.state}return true}function eq(a,b){if(typeof a!==typeof b)return false;if(a===null||b===null)return a===b;if(Array.isArray(a)){if(!Array.isArray(b)||a.length!==b.length)return false;for(let i=0;i<a.length;i++)if(!eq(a[i],b[i]))return false;return true}if(typeof a==='object'){let x=Object.keys(a),y=Object.keys(b);if(x.length!==y.length)return false;for(let k of x)if(!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(b,k)||!eq(a[k],b[k]))return false;return true}return a===b}
initial.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(!s)s={a:c.initial,sp:0,r:[],g:[],t:[]};var st='invalid',id=e&&e.id,ty=e&&e.type,amt=e&&e.amount,validId=typeof id==='string',pos=Number.isSafeInteger(amt)&&amt>0;function idx(a,k){for(var i=0;i<a.length;i++)if(a[i].id===k)return i;return -1}function grant(k){return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(c.grants,k)}if(ty==='receive'&&validId&&pos){var gi=grant(id),rv=s.g.indexOf(id);if(rv>=0)st=(amt===c.grants[id]?'duplicate':'invalid');else if(gi&&amt===c.grants[id]){s.g.push(id);s.a+=amt;st='accepted'}}else if((ty==='send'||ty==='spend')&&validId&&pos){var j=idx(s.t,id);if(j>=0)st=s.t[j].amt===amt?'duplicate':'conflict';else if(s.a<amt)st='insufficient';else{s.a-=amt;s.t.push({id:id,amt:amt,p:ty==='send'});if(ty==='spend')s.sp+=amt;st='accepted'}}else if((ty==='ack'||ty==='cancel')&&validId){var q=idx(s.t,id);if(q>=0&&s.t[q].p){s.t[q].p=false;if(ty==='cancel')s.a+=s.t[q].amt;st='accepted'}else st='ignored'}var p=[],r=s.g.slice();for(var z=0;z<s.t.length;z++)if(s.t[z].p)p.push(s.t[z].id);p.sort();r.sort();return{state:s,output:{available:s.a,spent:s.sp,pending:p,received:r,status:st}}}

final.explanation: Accepted receives add each listed grant once. Fresh sends and spends debit available once; spends increase spent, while sends remain permanently recorded and are refundable only while pending. Acknowledging a pending send makes it delivered without refund; cancelling refunds exactly once. Receive, send, and spend identities use separate namespaces, and all reported identity arrays are sorted by Unicode code points.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s===null){s={a:c.initial,sp:0,g:[],sn:[],wn:[]}}var ty=e&&e.type,id=e&&e.id,amt=e&&e.amount,st='invalid',has=typeof id==='string',pos=Number.isSafeInteger(amt)&&amt>0;function own(o,k){return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o,k)}function find(a,k){for(var i=0;i<a.length;i++)if(a[i].id===k)return i;return-1}function cp(a,b){var x=Array.from(a),y=Array.from(b),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(var i=0;i<n;i++){var u=x[i].codePointAt(0),v=y[i].codePointAt(0);if(u!==v)return u-v}return x.length-y.length}function sorted(a){return a.sort(cp)}if(ty==='receive'&&has&&pos){var gi=own(c.grants,id),ri=s.g.indexOf(id);if(ri>=0)st=amt===c.grants[id]?'duplicate':'invalid';else if(gi&&amt===c.grants[id]){s.g.push(id);s.a+=amt;st='accepted'}}else if((ty==='send'||ty==='spend')&&has&&pos){var ar=ty==='send'?s.sn:s.wn,j=find(ar,id);if(j>=0)st=ar[j].amt===amt?'duplicate':'conflict';else if(s.a<amt)st='insufficient';else{s.a-=amt;ar.push({id:id,amt:amt});if(ty==='send')ar[ar.length-1].p=true;else s.sp+=amt;st='accepted'}}else if((ty==='ack'||ty==='cancel')&&has){var k=find(s.sn,id);if(k>=0&&s.sn[k].p){s.sn[k].p=false;if(ty==='cancel')s.a+=s.sn[k].amt;st='accepted'}else st='ignored'}var p=[],r=s.g.slice();for(var z=0;z<s.sn.length;z++)if(s.sn[z].p)p.push(s.sn[z].id);sorted(p);sorted(r);return{state:s,output:{available:s.a,spent:s.sp,pending:p,received:r,status:st}}}

initial.explanation: Maintain separate receive, send, and spend identity records. Debits occur on accepted sends/spends; pending sends refund only on cancellation. Outputs are rebuilt with code-point ordering.
initial.mapping: The optional rule maps available and spent to conserved rights, received grants to additions, and pending sends to reserved debits. Transfer of the outside archival-order rule is inappropriate because this task defines operational identity and ordering, not provenance.
initial.assumptions: Malformed receive/send/spend operations are invalid. Ack and cancel operations that do not target a currently pending send are ignored, including malformed targets.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){var c=input.config,total=c.initial;for(var o of output){if(!o||typeof o.available!='number'||typeof o.spent!='number'||o.available<0||o.spent<0)return false;var g=0;for(var id of o.received||[])if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(c.grants,id))g+=c.grants[id];if(o.available+o.spent>total+g)return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s===null){s={a:c.initial,sp:0,r:[],se:[],pe:[],sc:[],ss:[]}}function has(a,id){return a.indexOf(id)>=0}function rec(a,id){for(var z of a)if(z[0]===id)return z;return null}function cmp(a,b){var x=Array.from(a),y=Array.from(b),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(var i=0;i<n;i++){if(x[i].codePointAt(0)!==y[i].codePointAt(0))return x[i].codePointAt(0)-y[i].codePointAt(0)}return x.length-y.length}var st='ignored',t=e&&e.type,id=e&&e.id,amt=e&&e.amount,validId=typeof id==='string';if(t==='receive'){if(!validId||typeof amt!=='number'||!Number.isSafeInteger(amt)||amt<=0||!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(c.grants,id)||c.grants[id]!==amt)st='invalid';else if(has(s.r,id))st='duplicate';else{s.r.push(id);s.a+=amt;st='accepted'}}else if(t==='send'||t==='spend'){var arr=t==='send'?s.se:s.ss,old=rec(arr,id);if(!validId||typeof amt!=='number'||!Number.isSafeInteger(amt)||amt<=0)st='invalid';else if(old)st=old[1]===amt?'duplicate':'conflict';else if(s.a<amt)st='insufficient';else{arr.push([id,amt]);s.a-=amt;if(t==='send')s.pe.push([id,amt]);else s.sp+=amt;st='accepted'}}else if(t==='ack'||t==='cancel'){if(validId){var q=rec(s.pe,id);if(q){s.pe.splice(s.pe.indexOf(q),1);if(t==='cancel')s.a+=q[1]}}}else st='invalid';var rr=s.r.slice().sort(cmp),pp=s.pe.map(function(z){return z[0]}).sort(cmp);return{state:s,output:{status:st,available:s.a,spent:s.sp,pending:pp,received:rr}}}

final.explanation: Tracks available rights, spent totals, received grants, permanently recorded sends/spends, and currently pending sends. Receive, send, and spend identities are separate. Accepted sends/spends debit immediately; cancellation refunds a pending send, while acknowledgment only removes pending status. Outputs sort identifiers by Unicode code point order.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s===null)s={a:c.initial,sp:0,r:[],se:[],pe:[],ss:[]};function find(a,id){for(var i=0;i<a.length;i++)if(a[i][0]===id)return a[i];return null}function has(a,id){return a.indexOf(id)>=0}function cmp(a,b){var i=0,n=Math.min(a.length,b.length);while(i<n){var x=a.codePointAt(i),y=b.codePointAt(i);if(x!==y)return x-y;i++}return a.length-b.length}var t=e&&e.type,id=e&&e.id,amt=e&&e.amount,st='ignored',ok=typeof id==='string';if(t==='receive'){if(!ok||typeof amt!=='number'||!Number.isSafeInteger(amt)||amt<=0||!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(c.grants,id)||c.grants[id]!==amt)st='invalid';else if(has(s.r,id))st='duplicate';else{s.r.push(id);s.a+=amt;st='accepted'}}else if(t==='send'||t==='spend'){var a=t==='send'?s.se:s.ss,o=find(a,id);if(!ok||typeof amt!=='number'||!Number.isSafeInteger(amt)||amt<=0)st='invalid';else if(o)st=o[1]===amt?'duplicate':'conflict';else if(s.a<amt)st='insufficient';else{a.push([id,amt]);s.a-=amt;if(t==='send')s.pe.push([id,amt]);else s.sp+=amt;st='accepted'}}else if(t==='ack'||t==='cancel'){if(ok){var p=find(s.pe,id);if(p){s.pe.splice(s.pe.indexOf(p),1);if(t==='cancel')s.a+=p[1]}}}else st='invalid';return{state:s,output:{status:st,available:s.a,spent:s.sp,pending:s.pe.map(function(v){return v[0]}).sort(cmp),received:s.r.slice().sort(cmp)}}}

initial.explanation: Maintain separate permanent receive, send, and spend identity maps. Successful debits are immediate; sends additionally enter pending, with acknowledgment consuming the reservation and cancellation refunding it once. Outputs are rebuilt with sorted identifiers after every event.
initial.mapping: The rule maps available and spent to ledger balances, grants to receivable rights, received to accepted grant IDs, and pending to undelivered successful sends. Separate maps preserve operation namespaces and conflict/duplicate history.
initial.assumptions: Event and configuration values are decoded JSON primitives within the stated limits. Invalid operation shapes receive invalid (or ignored for control operations lacking a valid ID).

final.explanation: Uses separate permanent records for receives, sends, and spends, so namespaces and historical conflicts remain isolated. Successful sends debit immediately and remain pending until acknowledgment or one-time cancellation refund. Receive duplicates require the original grant amount; mismatches are invalid. Outputs rebuild sorted identifier arrays after each event.
